messages.subject: Jolly-Seber m-array likelihood
parts: I have been working to fit a Jolly-Seber model to individual-level capture histories in a state-space formulation following chapter 10 of the BPA book (K&S 2012).  My target of interest is abundance estimation, so I have been employing data augmentation throughout this process.  I am now interested in fitting the model for a large capture-history data set (dimensions: ~7000 rows, 500 cols).  I have some flexibility in analysis, as I am not interested in individual-level effects.  Because of this, I would like to translate the state-space likelihood of the Jolly-Seber to the m-array formulation, but I have had considerable trouble working through this conversion.  I am aware of the likelihood's generalized expression in chapter 18 of "the brown book" (WNC 2002), but have still struggled with translating this for use in JAGS in a format robust to work through my dataset.  Is anyone aware of where the m-array likelihood of any Jolly-Seber parameterization has been worked out in BUGS?

messages.author: af31ce3a70c4aa9e
messages.subject: Re: Jolly-Seber m-array likelihood
parts:
Hi Taylor,

A tutorial script is attached I put together for a methods paper we're writing. From Schaub and Kery (2022; IPM book) as well as Saracco and Yackulic (2023; bioRXiv).

In the script we also include a robust design based on some papers Dan Gibson and I wrote a while ago, although that's not technically necessary. Please note that given the number of occasions you have (500?) this may take a very long time to run with any approach, and I bet Saracco and Yackulic's approach may be faster than the m-array, although that tends to vary given what the data look like.

Best wishes,

Thomas
